reading.text:
Reading for lpMeasurableSpace (used by Ass 2.2 and many other claims).
Paper: L^2(nu; R^j) is a separable Hilbert space (E countably generated, nu sigma-finite); the jump
coefficient's measurability (2.2) is Borel measurability into L^2(nu;R^n); H's laws use the Borel
sigma-field of H, whose U-coordinate is L^2(nu;R^m). So the measurable structure on L^2(nu;R^j)
must be its Borel sigma-field for the norm topology (equivalently, since separable, the sigma-field
generated by the maps u |-> <u, v> or by open balls). Faithful Lean: MeasurableSpace instance on
Lp (R^j-valued, p = 2, nu) equal to borel (Lp ...). A different choice (top, or a sigma-field
generated by something else) would change measurability requirements and laws.

comparison.text:
Comparison for lpMeasurableSpace (System/Tuple.lean:65): a scoped instance MeasurableSpace (Lp F 2 nu) :=
borel _, the Borel sigma-algebra of the norm topology of L^2(nu; F) (with the companion BorelSpace
instance).
Against my reading (L^2(nu; R^j) carries its Borel sigma-field, needed for (2.2), for laws on H and for
P_2(L^2(nu))): exact match. Being scoped to the namespace, it is the instance every PaperSpec
statement opening that namespace sees (the claims are stated with it in scope). For countably
generated E and sigma-finite nu, L^2(nu) is second countable (the file's fact instance), so this Borel
sigma-field equals the one generated by the open balls / weak functionals, as the paper uses.
Verdict: faithful.
